steps.description: A 3x3 grid. First join every land cell to its land neighbours, so each island becomes one set that knows its size.
Land (0,0) and land (0,1) touch, so they are one island. unionBySize(0, 1): roots 0 and 1. Set 0 is at least as big, so 1 hangs under it.
Land (0,0) and land (1,0) touch, so they are one island. unionBySize(0, 3): roots 0 and 3. Set 0 is at least as big, so 3 hangs under it.
Land (1,2) and land (2,2) touch, so they are one island. unionBySize(5, 8): roots 5 and 8. Set 5 is at least as big, so 8 hangs under it.
Land (2,1) and land (2,2) touch, so they are one island. unionBySize(7, 8): roots 7 and 5. Set 5 is bigger, so 7 hangs under it.
Flipping water (0,2) joins 2 distinct islands: 1 + 3 + 3 = 7. maxSize = 7.
Flipping water (1,1) joins 2 distinct islands: 1 + 3 + 3 = 7. maxSize = 7.
Flipping water (2,0) joins 2 distinct islands: 1 + 3 + 3 = 7. maxSize = 7.
The best flip gives an island of 7. Return maxSize.
